item.title: FG disburses N75bn to 104 manufacturers, N65.8bn to MSMEs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs. Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”. Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth. The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs. The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses. Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026. She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone. The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment. She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness. According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive. Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent. “Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said. The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent. item.title: 2027: Umrah won’t guarantee Tinubu second term — Phrank Shaibu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has said President Bola Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia for Umrah will not guarantee his re-election in 2027. Shaibu criticised the President’s religious pilgrimage, saying a second term in office could not be secured through spiritual claims. The spokesperson for ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. Shaibu said visiting the holy land should be a personal affair rather than a national event, accusing Tinubu’s supporters of politicising the pilgrimage. He also questioned the President’s sincerity of faith, arguing that former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, would not remain in custody if Tinubu genuinely practised what he professed. Shaibu further criticised Tinubu for speaking into a microphone in Saudi Arabia while Nigerians were struggling with economic hardship. He dismissed the administration’s claims of economic improvement, saying many Nigerians continued to face difficult living conditions. According to him, Nigerians would remember the President’s prayers in Mecca alongside the high cost of food, goods and services. Asked whether Atiku would have accompanied Tinubu to Saudi Arabia if invited, Shaibu said the former vice-president had sponsored the President’s first trip to Mecca. On Atiku’s chances in the 2027 presidential election across the northern states, the ADC campaign spokesman expressed confidence in the former vice-president’s prospects, saying he was “home and dry” in the region. Tinubu departed Abuja for Makkah on October 29 to perform Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Speaking to journalists after completing the religious rites, the President described the pilgrimage as a fulfilling spiritual experience and an opportunity to pray for the country. Tinubu said he had asked God for wisdom and resilience to continue leading Nigerians, expressing confidence that his prayers had been answered. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted,” he said. The President recalled performing Umrah before the 2023 election, saying he had returned to thank Allah for granting his earlier prayer. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah,” Tinubu said. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, ‘Use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person,’” he added. item.title: SUNU Assurances, SUNU Health strengthen breast cancer awareness
item.description: SUNU Assurances Nigeria PLC and SUNU Health Nigeria Limited, in collaboration with H2O Wellness Foundation, has sensitised over 60 women including 40 radio presenters, on breast cancer awareness, focusing on early detection and preventive healthcare, urging them to prioritise their health while educating the public. Speaking during the initiative in Lagos, tagged ‘Pink Mic 2026’, Convener of the H2O Wellness campaign and broadcast journalist, Janet Karz Joshua, said the initiative was designed to address the need for women in the media industry to pay greater attention to their health, despite their responsibility to educate and inform the public. Joshua said women journalists regularly use their platforms to promote breast cancer awareness but often neglect their personal health needs in the process. According to her, the initiative was established to ensure that female media practitioners receive the information, medical attention and support needed to make informed decisions about their wellbeing. She said the maiden edition was organised to equip participants with practical knowledge they could take back to their respective media organisations and use to educate wider audiences. Joshua added that the foundation would measure the programme’s impact by encouraging participants to sustain conversations about breast health and preventive healthcare through their radio programmes, news reports and other media platforms. She explained that the campaign would also explore opportunities to engage women across different professions and socioeconomic backgrounds, stressing that healthcare awareness should be accessible to everyone. “Women in the media give information, but are we cared for the way we should be cared for?” she asked, explaining the motivation behind the campaign.” Joshua said. In her remarks, the Head of Corporate Services, SUNU Assurances, Japari Yusuf, said breast cancer awareness must go beyond annual campaigns to become a regular part of conversations among families, workplaces and communities. Yusuf, who spoke on behalf of SUNU Assurances and SUNU Health, said the organisation supported the initiative because of its commitment to preventive healthcare, access to medical services and community wellbeing. Yusuf also recalled losing a colleague to breast cancer in 2018 after the woman underwent chemotherapy and initially appeared to be recovering. Yusuf said SUNU Group’s participation was part of its Pink October campaign, adding that the organisation had previously supported breast cancer screening for 100 women in 2024 and 150 women in 2025. Also speaking, the Founder and Medical Director of HealthRite Company Limited, Dr. Uchenna Anekwuonye, called for greater attention to lifestyle medicine, physical activity and other evidence-based approaches to maintaining good health. item.title: BUA Foods expands margin as profit rises to N450bn
item.description: A leading Nigerian food manufacturing company, BUA Foods Plc, has recorded an increase in gross profit to N552.90 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, compared with N520.65 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gross profit margin expanded significantly to 48.3%, from 36.7% in the prior-year period, reflecting improved cost efficiency and disciplined cost management. The strong margin performance supported an 11% year-on-year increase in profit after tax to N450.47 billion, up from N405.27 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. The Company’s unaudited financial results demonstrate the resilience of its operating model and the impact of disciplined cost management, with profitability improving amid evolving market dynamics and a continued focus on operational efficiency. A key driver of performance was the 34% reduction in cost of sales to N592.94 billion, reflecting lower topline costs and a more stable foreign exchange environment. Further demonstrating improved operating efficiency, total operating expenses decreased by 20% to N66.99 billion, compared with N83.65 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Selling and distribution expenses declined by 15% to N45.04 billion, while administrative expenses reduced by 28% to N21.95 billion. These improvements supported a 12-percentage-point expansion in operating profit margin, which rose to 43% from 31%. Profit before tax grew by 11% to N480.52 billion, while Earnings per share also increased by 11% to N25.03, compared with N22.52 in the prior-year period. Commenting on the results, Engr. Ayodele Abioye, Managing Director of BUA Foods Plc, said: “Our nine-month 2026 results demonstrate the resilience of BUA Foods’ operating model and the benefits of disciplined cost and margin management. Despite a 19% decline in revenue to N1.15 trillion, driven by softer pricing conditions and subdued consumer demand, we maintained a substantial improvement in profitability through effective cost optimisation, improved productivity and rigorous execution across the business. “The sustained strength of our brands and our continued investment in route-to-market capabilities provide a solid foundation for future growth. ‘‘Looking ahead, we remain focused on driving profitable growth, enhancing market penetration and maintaining operational efficiency. ‘‘While the operating environment remains dynamic, BUA Foods is well-positioned to leverage its scale, strong market positions and execution capabilities to deliver sustainable long-term value.” The post BUA Foods expands margin as profit rises to N450bn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reforms laid foundation for Nigeria’s sugar self-sufficiency — NSDC Boss
item.description: The Executive Secretary/CEO of the National Sugar Development Council (NSDC), Mr. Kamar Bakrin, has said the bold, macroeconomic reforms put in place by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu have made local sugar production attractive and cleared the pathway for the country to achieve self-sufficiency. Bakrin was speaking as a panelist at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NESG #32), on the topic, “Strengthening Policy Coordination for the Non-alcoholic Drink Sector Competitiveness.” He said the reforms have brought stability to the economy, adding that the next step is to turn stability into growth that works for ordinary Nigerians. He stated further: “Our most pressing priorities are well known: jobs, especially for young people; rural livelihoods; security; pressure on foreign exchange; food security; and the cost of living. “Every Government must make choices among competing priorities. Our contribution as a Council is to make sure that, when those choices are made, the full economic picture of the sugar value chain is on the table. This is because very few sectors touch all of these priorities at once the way sugar does.” Responding to the Summit’s theme of turning stability into growth that works for ordinary Nigerians, he said sugar offers a practical route. Under the Nigeria Sugar Master Plan (NSMP) 2.0, the goal is self-sufficiency in sugar production. Bakrin said reaching it would save about $1 billion in foreign exchange every year and create about 110,000 direct jobs, most of them in rural communities, on estates, in mills and on outgrower farms where smallholders grow cane for the mills. “The gains go beyond the factory gate. Sugar estates bring roads, schools, clinics and electricity generated from bagasse, the fibre left after cane is crushed’’. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 3, 2026
item.description: The naira traded at approximately ₦1,347.44 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the US dollar sold for about ₦1,395 in the parallel market on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The latest official NFEM rate represents the most recent available market quotation, while parallel-market rates vary depending on location and currency dealers. In the parallel market, Bureau de Change operators quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,395 for selling. At these rates, $100 exchanges for approximately ₦134,744 at the official market and ₦139,500 at the parallel market. The difference between the official and parallel-market selling rates is about ₦47.56 per dollar. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with authorised dealers before conducting foreign exchange transactions. item.title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
item.description: •Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges By Peter Egwuatu Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems. A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024. The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms. Demand deposits rise 71% Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023. The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025. The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand. Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system. ‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system. ‘‘Their growth rates alone do not establish how much of the increase in cash holdings is attributable to economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changes in payment preferences.” The post Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State. In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027. She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face. Excerpts: You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision? I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it. I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate. What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office? The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers. Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition. However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately. Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong? I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities. item.title: 2027: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse — Mutfwang
item.description: •Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition. Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed. Governor Mutfwang said: “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain. Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’ On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. item.title: Give Tinubu, Otu another term for Bakassi seaport, coastal highway — Shettima
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar. He thanked the people of Cross River for supporting the administration over the past three years, describing the relationship between the government and the electorate as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity.” “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. The Vice President urged voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu, Otu and APC candidates seeking election into the National Assembly and the state House of Assembly. He said the party was seeking another mandate based on its stewardship, stressing that elected officials must account to the people who entrusted them with power. On infrastructure, Shettima said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would link coastal communities, ease the movement of goods and people, boost tourism and attract investment to the region. He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy. On education, he said the government’s student financing initiative would promote human capital development, reduce the financial burden on parents and expand access to higher education. item.title: YPP’s Agada wants end to raw material exports
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits. Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export. “The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said. He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange. “Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said. The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home. He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness. On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels. He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past. item.title: Customs appoints Mamman Ali acting Adamawa/Taraba Comptroller
item.description: By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command. Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna. At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure. He said the command strengthened security along critical border corridors through enhanced joint operations and patrols with sister security agencies. Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190. He commended officers and men of the command for their cooperation during his tenure and urged them to extend the same support to his successor. In his remarks, the new Acting Area Comptroller, Ali, pledged to build on the achievements of his predecessor. He solicited the support and cooperation of sister security agencies, officers and men of the command to strengthen border policing and curb smuggling activities across Adamawa and Taraba states. item.title: Kefas’ education reforms could make Taraba N-Nigeria’s learning hub—CCDI
item.description: THE Centre for Convention on Democratic Integrity, CCDI, has lauded the education reforms of Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, saying they could position the state as a leading centre of educational excellence in Northern Nigeria. The organisation also urged the World Bank and United Nations agencies to support the state’s education sector through technical assistance, appropriate financing and institutional partnerships. A statement by CCDI’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), Olufemi Aduwo, said the administration’s invesment in education was fundamental to Taraba’s long-term prosperity and the competitiveness of its young people. Aduwo, recently elected Vice-President of the World Bank Civil Society Policy Forum (CSPF), said the organisation’s assessment team on the Sustainable Development Goals, which visited Taraba in September, took particular note of the implementation of free and compulsory primary and secondary education. He listed the payment of WAEC, NECO and NABTEB examination fees, reduced tuition at Taraba State University and nursing schools, and the establishmentof model schools where pupils receive uniforms, textbooks and footwear among the interventions that should serve as a wake-up call to other states. He added that the sponsorship of indigenes for postgraduate studies abroad, increased support for medical students and bursaries for law students further demonstrated the administration’s commitment to expanding educational opportunities. Aduwo said the initiatives represented a significant milestone in Taraba’s development since its creation in 1991, urging the government to sustain the momentum and ensure that improved access was matched by higher teaching standards. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses INEC list omission
item.description: ….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta. The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party. The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state. Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards. He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party. “We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said. Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State. item.title: Diri urges Bayelsa governorship aspirants to seek God
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person. Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God. He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs. The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development. Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government. “All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said. He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day. “As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks. “We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.” In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship. Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society. Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship. The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office. He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination. He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership. item.title: 2027: Osamaye arms Ifedore wards with PAS, N1m for mobilisation
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Ondo State Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Dr Seun Osamaye, has boosted grassroots structures in Ifedore Local Government with 11 public address systems and N1 million support. The items were presented at a strategic meeting where Osamaye hosted all ward chairmen, ward secretaries and the Executive Chairman of Ifedore Local Government. The gathering focused on strengthening party coordination, deepening political engagement at ward level and mapping out strategies for effective mobilisation before the 2027 polls. Osamaye said the public address systems would solve communication challenges at the grassroots, especially during ward meetings, community engagements and political activities. She told the leaders that she sees her appointment as holding Ifedore’s slot in the State Executive Council, and that she remains committed to projecting the council’s interest. While thanking Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and the First Lady, Mrs Oluwaseun Aiyedatiwa, for the opportunity to serve, she urged Ifedore leaders to reciprocate with total support for the administration. According to her, the build-up to 2027 requires unity among ward leaders, constant presence in communities and clear dissemination of government policies and party programmes. She charged them to work for the success of the party at all levels, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second term bid, as evidence that Governor Aiyedatiwa has mobilised the state’s political structure effectively. In his remarks, Ifedore Local Government Chairman, Hon. Prince Tunde Adegbonmire, described Osamaye as a proud ambassador of the council whose performance in the cabinet has given Ifedore visibility.. Adegbonmire described Osamaye as a worthy representative of Ifedore at the state level, noting that her service in Governor Aiyedatiwa’s administration has brought recognition to the local government. He acknowledged her efforts in maintaining strong ties with political stakeholders in the council and creating opportunities for grassroots leaders to engage with the state government. The council chairman appreciated the donation of the public address systems and financial support, describing it as an intervention that would assist the local government and its wards in carrying out activities. He assured the commissioner of continued cooperation with Governor Aiyedatiwa’s political structure, adding that the ward leadership would work to strengthen mobilisation, coordination and participation across the local government. Adegbonmire further assured that Ifedore LG would collaborate with relevant party stakeholders to support the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 elections. The ward chairmen also expressed commitment to collaboration, unity, effective communication and sustained engagement as preparations for the 2027 general elections continue. outreach. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu’s Aide Refutes Claim President Visited Saudi Arabia To Get Northern Votes
item.description: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Foreign Affairs and Protocol, Ademola Oshodi, has dismissed claims that the President visited Mecca in Saudi Arabia to curry favour with northerners, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Oshodi, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, said the trip was strictly religious as the President is a Muslim. The aide said that Tinubu’s presence in Mecca was not political, adding that even an opposition governor, Bala Mohammed of Bauchi State, was also present as a Muslim. He advised other presidential candidates in the 2027 general elections to also seek favour from God. The presidential aide said that though Nigerians are going through hardship, Tinubu is working to make things better. The President arrived in Saudi Arabia on October 29 and performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. After completing the rites, he said that he felt fulfilled. Tinubu, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections, also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson
item.description: Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, saying a second term in office cannot be guaranteed via a spiritual claim. The spokesperson for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. Shaibu said that visiting the holy land should be a personal affair and not national, accusing Tinubu’s supporters of politicising the event. ﻿ He questioned the President’s faith, saying former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, would not remain in custody if Tinubu had sincerity of faith. Shaibu also accused the President of speaking into a mic in Saudi Arabia while Nigerians “are dying of hunger”. He said that Tinubu administration’s claim that the economy has improved is false, as many Nigerians are facing hardship. According to him, Nigerians will remember Tinubu’s prayer in Mecca the same way they remember the high prices of food, goods and services. Asked whether Atiku would have accompanied Tinubu to Saudi Arabia if he had been invited, the aide said that the former vice president sponsored the President’s first trip to Mecca. On the chances of the ADC candidate in the 2027 presidential election across the northern states, Shaibu said Atiku is home and dry in the region. Tinubu departed Abuja for Makkah on October 29, where he performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Speaking shortly after completing the religious rites, which he described as a spiritual experience and an opportunity to pray for Nigeria, the President said he felt fulfilled. The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, ‘Use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person,’ Tinubu told journalists. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the President of this great country.” The post [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: NASS Considering Proposal To Create 74 Seats For Women, Says Bamidele
item.description: Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, on Monday disclosed that the National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) had proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives Bamidele, also Vice Chairman, Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, further revealed that the committee had proposed three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. He made this disclosure at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter on Monday, noting that the proposals were designed to deepen the inclusion of women in the country’s politics and governance process. A file photo of Senator Opeyemi Bamidele Ekiti FIDA, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the programme with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” Bamidele attended the programme alongside the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Steve Fatoba, and Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, among others. “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly,” Bamidele said. He further explained the centerpiece of the legislative initiative, which, according to him, was designed to create special seats for women at the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution. He added that the legislative initiative “is the fruit of extensive consultation and consensus-building. “It is why we commenced the constitutional amendment process early, ensuring that this is not a rushed, haphazard endeavour but a deliberate, inclusive, and thorough reform. “The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he added. Bamidele further revealed that the constitution review committee “has already proposed three additional seats for each state House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review.
